newsitem.title: FINLAND: Neste to emphasise gas business - CEO.
newsitem.headline: Neste to emphasise gas business - CEO.

text.p: Finnish oil and energy group Neste Oy will steer increasingly into the natural gas business, the group's chairman and CEO Jaakko Ihamuotila said on Friday.

"Neste will become more of a gas company," Ihamuotila told a news conference after Neste reported a 59 percent drop in 1996 earnings to 566 million markka ($112.4 million) -- the result weighed down by heavy losses in oil trading.

"Last year was significant for Neste in the gas business because of the start-up of our own natural gas production," Ihamuotila said, referring to production at the Heidrun field off the coast of Norway.

Besides its gas network in Finland, Neste's gas-related projects include developing the Asgard field off the Norwegian coast, its participation in gas production in Sweden and a projected pipeline to carry Russian gas via Finland to Europe.

Neste has a seven percent stake in the Asgard gas and oil field, which has known gas reserves of 191 billion cubic metres and is expected to be in oil production next year and in gas production in 2000, Neste said.
The other participants in the field are Norwegian Statoil as operator, Norsk Agip, Saga Petroleum ASA, Mobil, and Total Norge, a Neste spokeswoman said.

Last month Neste reached an agreement with Russian gas giant Gazprom to study the feasibility of a pipeline to carry gas to Europe -- possibly via Finland and southern Sweden or by a direct subsea route.
The feasibility study is expected to take two years, and building the pipeline would take a further five or six years, Neste spokesman Matti Saarinen said.

"Of course, it would be a big transfer business," Saarinen said. "Finland now imports about 3.5 billion cubic metres of gas annually. Gazprom has said it would like to put through 30 to 40 billion cubic metres."
"Without any doubt gas is the sector -- perhaps the only sector -- that will grow. It will grow even without a Nordic route," he said.

The onset this year of a discussion over Finland's future energy policy, Sweden's recent decision to phase out nuclear power capacity and concern over global climate change would contribute to a sharper focus on gas, Ihamuotila said.
